title: Is Hotel Fixture right for you?

turns.speaker: advisor
turns.text: Hotel Fixture. There's one thing to understand first: this place is about the view and the quiet, and little else gets in the way.

turns.speaker: traveler
turns.text: Which sounds great, but let's see who it really works for.

turns.speaker: advisor
turns.text: Start with the rooms. There are only 40, and every one has its own terrace facing the sea. You wake up and the water is right there.

turns.speaker: traveler
turns.text: And the beach is the part people talk about, right?

turns.speaker: advisor
turns.text: It is. There's a lift through the cliff down to a private beach. Dinner uses produce from their own terraced garden.

turns.speaker: traveler
turns.text: So this is a couples place. Somewhere you go to slow down and eat well.

turns.speaker: advisor
turns.text: Exactly. Couples and anyone who plans a trip around food will love it.

turns.speaker: traveler
turns.text: Two things I'd tell a client. It closes in winter, roughly November to March. And getting into town means a boat or a steep walk with a lot of steps.

turns.speaker: advisor
turns.text: Fair. If you want to be out exploring every night, that gets old. If you want to stay put, it's a feature.

turns.speaker: traveler
turns.text: Bottom line: book it for the view, the beach and the table, not nightlife.

short_version.worth_knowing: Closed in winter; town is a boat ride or steep walk away
